battle.name: 996年諾曼第農民起義
battle.brief: 996年諾曼第公爵理查二世遠赴意大利期間，貝桑與科區的農民起兵，奪取莊園武器、攻擊城堡，公爵回師後以封建徵召兵力平定，首領被處死，莊園被沒收。卡面的埃及長矛屬青銅時代工藝，與本役相隔三千年，並未在此役出現；當時諾曼步兵用鐵矛長槍，騎士用長矛、圓盾與騎槍。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 996年諾曼第農民起義，發生於西法蘭克王國境內的諾曼第公國，是公爵領地與教堂領地的農民對公爵理查二世的一次大規模武裝抗命。公國一方以十世紀初成形不久的「公告徵召」（ban）制度召集全境軍隊：骨幹是數百名持有騎槍、長矛與盾牌的騎士及其附庸，配以各莊園調出的步兵與民團，總指揮由公爵本人與公國官員共同掌握；子爵（vicomte）與總管（bailli）分掌司法、徵收與調發，貝桑的王室莊園與城塞、科區沿岸的海濱堡壘由公爵直屬的守備官把持。起義方並非獨立國家，而是散居於貝桑平原與科區丘陵的農民社群，分屬公爵直轄領地、貝桑與孔坦斯兩處主教區以及魯昂總主教區的教產田莊，多為持有小型自由地或租佃份地的武裝農人，起事後以村社為單位集結，用村莊內的農具、獵具與長矛成軍。第三方則有法蘭西國王羅貝爾二世——諾曼第公爵在法理上仍是他的臣屬，必要時可向國王求援；教會同時是受損的地主與調解的權威，魯昂總主教與各主教握有譴責、贖罪與仲裁之權。背景中還有北方丹麥與挪威的襲擾，使剛完成重墾的沿海平原始終處於戒備狀態。
countriesEn: The peasant rising of 996 took place inside the Duchy of Normandy in the West Frankish kingdom and was a large-scale armed defiance of Duke Richard II by the peasants of both the ducal and the ecclesiastical estates. The ducal side mobilised through the ban, the proclamation levy that had only taken shape in the early tenth century: its backbone was several hundred knights with lances, spears and shields together with their retinues, supported by infantry and militia drawn from the manors, while overall command lay with the duke in person and with the ducal officials. Viscounts and stewards divided the work of justice, taxation and levies between them, and the royal manors and castles of the Bessin and the coastal strongholds of the Caux were held by captains directly responsible to the duke. The insurgents were not a state but rural communities scattered across the Bessin plain and the Caux hills; they belonged to the duke's own demesne, to the bishoprics of Bayeux and Coutances and to the archbishopric of Rouen, and most were armed peasants holding small freehold or tenement plots who, once they rose, mustered by village community and armed themselves with the tools, hunting weapons and spears of the countryside. Third parties included the Frankish king Robert II, to whom the duke of Normandy remained a vassal in law and from whom he could call for aid, and the Church, which was at once the injured landlord and the authority of mediation: the archbishop of Rouen and the bishops held the powers of censure, penance and arbitration. In the background stood Danish and Norwegian raiding from the north, keeping the freshly resettled coastal plain in a state of permanent alert.
people: 關鍵人物集中在公爵一側。理查二世（約九五八至一〇二六年），綽號「良善者」，父親是「弓箭手」理查一世，母親居爾諾爾出身諾曼世家，它在十世紀後半確立了吉爾諾王朝的權力，並在九六〇年前後促成與法蘭西王室的和解。理查二世九八七年迎娶布盧瓦的艾瑪，九九八年得子威廉，此子即後來的征服者威廉；他本人則在九九六年因前妻朱迪特去世而遠赴意大利朝聖，行程與起義爆發的時間重疊。留守期間主持政務的是魯昂總主教羅伯特，他是公爵最親信的助手，也是各地領主與主教的仲裁人。各主教區的武裝力量由主教與座堂參事調動，貝桑與孔坦斯兩區的主教，以及管理貝桑王室莊園的公爵直屬官員，都是平叛時的關鍵節點人物。起義方則幾乎沒有留下姓名：編年史只以「村社首領」「最先煽動者」一類的稱呼指稱他們，個別首領被記為在公爵歸來後被捕、處死或流放，沒有一人留下較完整的傳記。後世追述此事的編年史家歐德里克·維塔利斯在十二世紀初的《教會史》中記錄了理查二世對叛亂者的嚴懲，成為今日了解這場起義的主要依據之一。
peopleEn: The key figures are concentrated on the duke's side. Richard II (c. 958-1026), surnamed the Good, was the son of Richard I the Archer and of Gunnor, who came from a great Norman house, established the power of the Gunnorid dynasty in the second half of the tenth century and brokered the reconciliation with the Frankish court around 960. Richard II married Emma of Blois in 987 and had a son William in 998, the child who would become the Conqueror; in 996 he himself set out for Italy on pilgrimage following the death of his first wife Judith, and the timing of that journey coincided with the outbreak of the revolt. Public affairs were conducted during his absence by Robert, archbishop of Rouen, his most trusted helper and the arbiter of the lords and bishops. The armed strength of the bishoprics was mustered by the bishops and the chapters of their cathedrals, and the bishops of Bayeux and Coutances, together with the ducal officer administering the royal manors of the Bessin, were the pivotal figures of the campaign of suppression. On the insurgent side almost no names survive: the chroniclers refer to the leaders only as village headmen or first instigators, and individual leaders are recorded as having been seized, executed or exiled once the duke returned, none of them leaving a fuller biography. The later chronicler Orderic Vitalis, writing the Ecclesiastical History in the early twelfth century, recorded the severity of Richard II's punishment of the rebels, and his account is one of the principal sources for the rising today.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬早王朝時期的工藝，銅或青銅矛頭以綁紮方式固定在木杆上，並未出現在九九六年的諾曼第戰場；它在此處代表的是「步兵長矛」這一兵器的原型與譜系起點。當時真正裝備部隊的是鐵矛：矛頭鑲嵌於梣木或白楊木的杆上，長度依使用者身高自一點六公尺到二公尺不等，諾曼步兵把矛握在身側、以盾護身，作為抵禦騎兵衝鋒的基本手段；騎士則用長得多的騎槍，槓身細長，衝鋒時夾在腋下。防護方面有諾曼式鎖子甲、帶鼻護的頭盔，以及木板包皮革的圓盾與日漸拉長的風箏盾。弓仍是步兵的重要武器，弩雖已有零星出土，仍屬獵具與圍攻用的稀有裝備。公國城堡多為土木寨牆加木構望樓，攻城時靠擲石機與壕溝、柵牆阻礙；遠征與平叛的補給靠牛車、馱馬與就地向莊園徵發的穀物、鹽與酒。起義者則大量使用農具改造的長柄武器，並從莊園與城堡的武器庫中奪取矛、斧與盾，這也是公爵其後明令禁止農民持矛的直接背景。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear shown on the card is a product of the early dynastic period, a copper or bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft, and it was never present on a Norman battlefield in 996; here it stands for the archetype and the pedigree of the infantry spear. What actually equipped the troops of the day was the iron spear: a socketed head set into a shaft of ash or poplar, its length running from about 1.6 to 2 metres according to the height of the bearer. Norman infantry held the spear at the side, covered by the shield, and it was their basic answer to a mounted charge; knights used a far longer cavalry lance of slight stock, tucked under the armpit when charging. Defensive equipment included mail of the Norman pattern, helmets with nasal pieces, and shields of wood faced with leather, round in form but lengthening into the kite shape. The bow remained an important infantry arm, and although the crossbow was already appearing sporadically in the record, it was still a rarity used for hunting and siege work. The ducal castles were mostly earthwork ramparts surmounted by wooden keeps, and sieges were shaped by stone-throwing engines, ditches and palisades; supply for campaigns and for the suppression of the revolt depended on ox carts, pack animals, and grain, salt and wine requisitioned on the spot from the manors. The insurgents used large numbers of long-handled tools adapted from farm implements, and they seized spears, axes and shields from the weapon stores of the manors and castles, which is the direct background to the duke's later ordinance forbidding peasants to bear arms.
tactics: 起義者的做法接近地方性騷亂而非會戰：他們趁公爵遠離、城堡守備空虛時夜行，先奪取莊園與城堡的武器庫，再打開監獄、燒毀莊園建築，切斷通向魯昂與卡昂的稅收驛道，並以村莊、教堂廣場與沼澤地帶作為集結與撤退的依靠；村社之間以口耳相傳聯絡，行動往往在數個村莊同時爆發，令公爵無法逐一定點。公國一側則以封建徵召的騎兵為突擊骨幹：公爵集結自願參戰的騎士與其隨從，選擇能讓騎兵展開的開闊地面，以長矛騎槍密集衝鋒，迫使聚集的起義者散開；步兵與民兵則結成以長矛與盾為主的密集隊形，在騎兵掩護下逐步把叛軍壓向河道渡口、橋樑與樹林地帶，逐村清剿。同時公爵切斷叛軍的糧食來源，封鎖其村社，破壞藏身莊園，並懸賞捉拿首領，以教堂禁令與贖罪程序施加宗教壓力。平定之後，公爵沒收起義者的土地，改封給新建的騎士據點，並以公告形式禁止農民攜帶長矛與刀劍，令私人武裝集中於受封的封建武士。
tacticsEn: The conduct of the insurgents was closer to a local rising than to a pitched battle. They moved by night while the duke was away and the castles were thin of garrison, seizing first the weapon stores of manors and castles, then opening the prisons, burning the manorial buildings, cutting the tax roads that led to Rouen and Caen, and using the villages, the churchyards and the marshy ground as both rallying point and place of refuge. The communities were linked by word of mouth, and the outbreak tended to happen simultaneously in several villages at once, so that the duke could not reduce them one point at a time. On the ducal side the shock force was the feudal levy of cavalry: the duke gathered the knights who came and their followers, chose ground on which the cavalry could deploy, and charged in a close line of lances, forcing the massed insurgents to scatter. Infantry and militia formed up in dense formations of spear and shield and, covered by the horse, pressed the rebels back towards river crossings, bridges and wooded country, clearing village by village. At the same time the duke cut the insurgents off from their food, sealed their communities in, destroyed the manors where they sheltered, posted rewards for the capture of the leaders, and applied religious pressure through church bans and the penitential process. Once the rising was suppressed, the duke confiscated the lands of the rebels, granted them to newly created knightly strongholds, and forbade peasants by public ordinance to carry spears, knives or swords, concentrating private arms in the hands of enfeoffed feudal warriors.
data: 關於這場起義，可靠的點名冊並不存在，數字只能作量級上的推估。編年史提到叛軍涵蓋「許多村莊」，而貝桑一地的聚落密度在《末日審查錄》時代以數百計，可見參與者來自整片鄉野而非單一莊園；史家一般認為直接起事的武裝農民在數百至數千人之間，首領人數只有個位數或十餘人，並有相當數量的未參與農戶被迫提供糧食與工具。公國方面的常備兵力有限，十世紀末諾曼第全部的騎士人數亦不過數百，公爵可支配的戰鬥人員主要靠臨時徵召，一般在數百騎加上同等數目的步兵這個量級。地理上，貝桑距魯昂約六十公里、距卡昂約一百公里，鄉村道路多為未鋪裝的泥路，堡壘之間的傳訊依賴騎馬，公爵的回師與調兵往往要花上數日。時間線上，起事被繫於九九六年，部分編年史把科區的騷動接續到翌年；至於公爵的行程與平定的季節，史料只說他在歸國途中聞訊後立即回師，具體月份並無記載。真正留下數字的是後果：被沒收的莊園數目與新封騎士的數目，都只能以「若干」「數十處」這類模糊的說法表述。
dataEn: No reliable roll of names survives for this rising, and its figures can only be estimated by order of magnitude. The chroniclers speak of the rebels as covering many villages, and since the number of settlements in the Bessin runs into the hundreds in the age of Domesday Book, the participants plainly came from a whole countryside rather than from any single manor. Historians generally put the armed peasants who rose directly at somewhere between several hundred and a few thousand, with the number of leaders in single figures or barely more than a dozen, and with a substantial body of non-participating households obliged to supply food and tools. The ducal side had no standing force to speak of: the total number of knights in late tenth-century Normandy was itself only a few hundred, and the fighting men the duke could dispose of depended on emergency levies, generally on the order of several hundred riders with a comparable number of foot. Geographically the Bessin lies about sixty kilometres from Rouen and about a hundred from Caen; the country roads were unpaved mud tracks, messages between strongholds travelled on horseback, and the duke's return and the concentration of troops commonly cost several days. Chronologically the outbreak is attached to 996, with some chroniclers carrying the disturbances in the Caux on into the following year; as for the duke's itinerary and the season of the suppression, the sources say only that he turned back as soon as he heard the news while on his way home, and give no month. The figures that survive are in the consequences: the number of manors confiscated and the number of knights newly enfeoffed can only be expressed in such vague terms as several or a number of places amounting to tens.
cause: 起義的直接背景是公爵外出留下的權力真空。理查二世九九六年因前妻之死與祈求子嗣而前往意大利與羅馬，往返數月，國政由魯昂總主教羅伯特主持，徵稅與司法卻未停頓，鄉間同時傳出公爵久去不歸、領地將被棄置的流言。更深層的壓力來自三方面：其一，貝桑與科區的農民既要向公爵與貴族繳納地租、雜稅與各類勞役，又要向教會繳納什一稅，兩套負擔疊加；其二，九七六至九七七年北歐的大饑荒餘波未平，歉收與飢餓的記憶仍留在鄉間，而宮廷開支與戰事徵發卻在增加；其三，九七九年前後洛林查理頒布的「城市徵召令」要求各城提供騎士，這類法令把軍役負擔進一步攤到地方，顯示王權與公國都在加緊抽取鄉村資源。同時，越來越平靜的局面讓農民得以積累武器——長矛、斧與獵弓；鄉村教堂與莊園庫房的看管也隨公爵遠行而鬆懈，提供了奪取武器的機會。
causeEn: The immediate background to the rising was the vacuum of authority left by the duke's journey. In 996 Richard II travelled to Italy and to Rome following the death of his first wife and in the hope of an heir, and during the months of his absence public affairs were conducted by Robert, archbishop of Rouen, while taxation and justice went on unbroken; at the same time rumours ran through the countryside that the duke was never coming back and that the land would be abandoned. The deeper pressure came from three quarters. First, the peasants of the Bessin and the Caux owed rents, dues and all manner of labour services to the duke and the nobles on top of the tithes owed to the Church, so that two systems of exaction were laid one upon the other. Second, the effects of the great famine of northern Europe in 976-77 had not yet worked themselves out; the memory of bad harvests and hunger was still fresh in the villages, while the costs of the court and of military levies went on rising. Third, ordinances of the kind issued around 979 by Charles of Lotharingia, requiring each city to furnish horsemen, pushed the burden of military service further down onto the localities, showing that both the royal and the ducal powers were tightening their grip on the countryside. At the same time, an increasingly peaceful situation allowed the peasants to accumulate weapons, spears, axes and hunting bows, and the guarding of village churches and manorial stores slackened with the duke's absence, providing the opportunity to seize them.
impact: 這場起義在諾曼第史上的意義，主要不在戰果，而在其後果的制度化。鎮壓之後，公國頒布限制農民攜帶武器的公告，被後世視為諾曼第農村軍事化受約束的關鍵節點：自此長矛、刀劍與獵弓的持有被視為領主與騎士的權利，鄉村的武力手段被壓縮成農具，農民自保的空間在接下來的一個多世紀裡持續收窄。沒收起義者土地、改封給新建騎士的做法，鞏固了十世紀末以來才剛建立的封建從屬網絡，把一批與中央關係較疏的莊園置於常駐的武裝據點之下，也加速了公國財政與軍役向盾錢與軍役合約的方向演變。從更大的背景看，維京對沿海平原的掠奪在九百年間告一段落，貝桑進入重墾與鞏固期，八九〇年代之後的第三代移民正把林地開墾成耕地；而一起以武裝抗命為形式的鄉村反叛被寫入編年史，也讓十二世紀以後的諾曼底史家不斷把這段記憶與普瓦捷的農民戰爭、卡佩王朝晚期的社會衝突並列，作為西洋封建社會早期「農民能否持械自衛」這一提問的第一個案例。
impactEn: The significance of this rising in Norman history lies less in its military outcome than in the institutional consequences that followed. After the suppression, the ducal ordinance restricting the carrying of weapons by peasants came to be regarded as the decisive point at which the military self-equipment of the Norman countryside was constrained: from then on the possession of spears, knives and bows was treated as the right of lords and knights, the armed means of the village were compressed back into farm tools, and the room for peasant self-defence continued to narrow over the more than a century that followed. The confiscation of the rebels' lands and their regranting to new knights consolidated the network of feudal dependency that had only just been built in the late tenth century, placed a number of manors that had stood at some distance from the centre under permanent armed strongholds, and accelerated the movement of ducal finance and military service towards scutage and the contractual service of knights. In a larger perspective, the Viking ravaging of the coastal plain had drawn to a close over the course of the ninth century and the Bessin had entered a phase of resettlement and consolidation, with the third generation of settlers after the 890s breaking woodland into farmland; and the fact that an armed rural defiance was written into the chronicles meant that Norman historians of the twelfth century and later repeatedly placed this memory alongside the peasant wars of Poitou and the social conflicts of the late Capetian monarchy, treating it as the first case of the western feudal question of whether peasants might bear arms in their own defence.
result: 結果是公爵方在全線取勝，起義在爆發後數月之內被壓平，沒有演變成持續的內戰。首領被逐一拘捕，記錄者稱其中數人被處死、數人被流放，受牽連的莊園被查抄，莊園上的人身權與土地權同時轉移，被重新分配給效忠公爵的騎士與其隨從。起義者賴以維生的村社並未被整體消滅，但村落的武裝被解除，長矛與刀劍被收繳或毀棄，教堂方面也配合宣布參與者的贖罪條件，將懲罰轉化為可以執行的教會程序。從公爵的立場看，這是一場代價不大的平叛：領土完整、封臣體系未受重創，魯昂總主教與各地主教仍能維持對鄉村的仲裁。從農民的立場看，結果卻更為嚴峻：他們的收成與地權沒有因此改善，徵稅與軍役負擔照舊，下一次大規模的抗爭要等到整整一個世紀之後，法國王室用城市徵召令把鄉村騎士調走的年代。這場起義因此成為十世紀末西歐最值得注意的一次鄉村武裝事件之一，既證明了諾曼第鄉村已能組織成軍，也同時暴露了公爵權力在鄉村中其實遠不如表面那樣穩固。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete ducal victory: the rising was crushed within months of the outbreak and never developed into a lasting civil war. The leaders were picked off one by one, and the recorders state that some were executed and others exiled; the manors implicated were confiscated, and both the personal and the land rights attaching to them were transferred and redistributed to knights loyal to the duke and their followers. The village communities on which the insurgents depended were not wiped out, but their arms were disarmed, spears and knives were surrendered or destroyed, and the Church cooperated by publishing the terms of penance for the participants, turning the punishment into a set of enforceable ecclesiastical procedures. From the duke's point of view this was a suppression bought at little cost: the territory was intact, the structure of the vassals was not badly damaged, and the archbishop of Rouen and the bishops of the province were still able to maintain their arbitration in the countryside. From the peasants' point of view the result was far harsher: neither their harvests nor their land rights improved, the burden of taxation and military service went on unchanged, and the next great resistance would not come until a full century later, in the age when the French crown began taking village horsemen away with the ban des villes. The rising therefore stands as one of the most remarkable rural armed incidents in western Europe in the late tenth century: it showed that the Norman countryside could already organise itself into an army, and at the same time exposed how much less secure the duke's power in the villages was than it appeared.
